problem_statement: J0SUKE X-Ray Visualizer is a Vite/TypeScript Three.js app with a fixed full-screen WebGL canvas, an OrbitControls + EffectComposer render pipeline, and an XRayEffect post-processing pass over a Lee Perry Smith head and a skeleton GLB. Above the scene, in the normal-flow #app overlay, sits the 'X-Ray Control HUD' section: a title, an 'X-Ray Layer' selector (Skin / Skeleton / Both tabs with a live 'Active layer' readout), and a readout chip row (Expand Lens, Shader Pipeline, Model Layer, Skeleton Layer, Viewport Resolution, Postprocessing Chain). The same X-Ray Layer selector also appears on the secondary /inspector.html view so the control stays consistent across the app. QA filed several defects on the current build: (1) on tablet (834px) and 390px mobile the HUD control rows are fixed-width no-wrap tracks that push past the viewport and force horizontal overflow, clipping the chips; (2) the X-Ray Layer selector is missing from the /inspector.html view, breaking cross-view consistency; (3) clicking a layer tab highlights it but the 'Active layer' readout never updates to the selected layer; and (4) the HUD panel styling has regressed so the chips shingle and overlap into an illegible strip that buries the top of the scene. Restore the HUD so its rows reflow inside tablet and mobile viewports with no horizontal overflow, the X-Ray Layer selector is present and consistent on both the home and inspector views, clicking a layer tab updates the live 'Active layer' readout, and the panel is legible again — while keeping the WebGL scene, the shader pipeline, the model/skeleton loaders, and the E-key expand interaction exactly as they are.
required_content: The X-Ray Control HUD rows (the X-Ray Layer selector row and the readout chip row) must not cause horizontal overflow on tablet (834px) or 390px mobile; documentElement.scrollWidth must stay within the viewport (tolerance 24px).
Keep the HUD content and its chips: X-Ray Control HUD, Expand Lens, Shader Pipeline, Model Layer, Skeleton Layer, Viewport Resolution, and Postprocessing Chain.
The X-Ray Layer selector (Skin / Skeleton / Both) with its 'Active layer' readout must be present and consistent on BOTH the home view and the /inspector.html view.

Clicking a layer tab must update the live 'Active layer' readout to the selected layer (for example 'Active layer: Skeleton · depth 2 of 3'); the readout must reflect the tab that was actually clicked, not a stale initial value.
The HUD panel must stay legible: chips must not shingle/overlap and text must remain readable; the panel must not bury the WebGL scene.

Keep the fixed full-screen WebGL canvas, the Lee Perry head model, the skeleton GLB, the color and normal textures, the x-ray fragment shader, EffectComposer/Bloom/X-Ray pass order, OrbitControls, mouse-driven lens behavior, and the E key expand interaction intact.
Do not introduce a new rendering framework, remote model source, external API, iframe, or unrelated UI shell to implement the fix.
design_constraints: Keep the app visually minimal: full-screen WebGL composition, small high-contrast overlay text, and mix-blend legibility should remain recognizable.
The HUD stays a lightweight technical overlay with compact rows, hairline-bordered chips, and short status labels; it is a section-level control/readout strip, not a dashboard or landing hero.
The overlay must not cover the face center, skeleton reveal area, or main lens window on desktop, tablet, or 390px mobile.
Use stable dimensions and wrapping so labels such as Viewport Resolution and Postprocessing Chain do not overflow on mobile.
The visual canvas remains primary; the HUD is a subordinate control/readout strip.
state_constraints: desktop_initial protects the default HUD layout, the X-Ray Layer selector, the fixed canvas, local GLB/texture loading, and WebGL rendering; the HUD already fits at desktop width and the panel is legible.
tablet_initial and mobile_initial capture the responsive defect: the fixed-width no-wrap HUD rows overflow the viewport horizontally.
desktop_layer_skeleton clicks the Skeleton layer tab and verifies the live 'Active layer' readout updates to the selected layer.
desktop_expand_key protects the existing E key interaction and verifies the HUD Expand Lens chip reflects the expanded lens state.

desktop_inspector, tablet_inspector, and mobile_inspector protect the /inspector.html view: the X-Ray Layer selector must be present and consistent there, and its rows must not overflow on tablet or mobile.

change_completion: The HUD control rows reflow so they fit inside tablet and mobile viewports with no horizontal overflow.
The X-Ray Layer selector and 'Active layer' readout are present on both the home and inspector views, and clicking a layer tab updates the readout to the selected layer.
design_consistency: The HUD stays minimal, high-contrast, legible, and subordinate to the full-screen WebGL scene, with chips that do not shingle or overlap.
The X-Ray Layer selector looks and behaves consistently across the home and inspector views.
regression: LeePerry and Skeleton loaders, local GLB/texture paths, model scale and positioning remain functional.
XRayEffect, XRayShader, the x-ray fragment shader, render target flow, EffectComposer pass order, OrbitControls, mouse-driven lens behavior, resize handling, and E key expansion remain functional.
responsive: Tablet and 390px mobile show the HUD with no horizontal overflow on both the home and inspector views.
The canvas remains fixed and correctly sized after the HUD reflows.

author_notes: Repair/regression_continuity task on the J0SUKE X-Ray Visualizer Vite/TypeScript Three.js demo. The native HUD lever is the app's own 'X-Ray Layer' selector (Skin / Skeleton / Both) rendered in the fixed-canvas overlay, with an 'Active layer' readout, present on the home view and the /inspector.html view. The full-screen WebGL canvas is position:fixed inset:0 and does not contribute to documentElement.scrollWidth, so the HUD control rows drive horizontal overflow independently of the scene. Four orthogonal gates discriminate the degraded legs: (D6) no_horizontal_overflow tolerance 24 on tablet/mobile home + inspector states; (D2) dom_assertions require the X-Ray Layer selector (xray-hud--inspector / xray-hud__tab / xray-hud__readout) on the inspector view; (D3) visual_regression (pixelmatch/ssim/block_fidelity over the HUD panel crops) catches the shingled/illegible panel; (D4) interaction_assertions require the 'Active layer' readout to update to the clicked layer. The leg-varying files are src/xray-hud.css (D6+D3), src/xray-hud-layer.js (D4), and the inspector.html page (D2). The reference passes all four. The baseline is the original defect set that keeps the fixed-width no-wrap rows (D6 overflow), drops the layer selector from the inspector view (D2), and looks visually distinct from the reference on the desktop states, but its layer-selector wiring is correct so it PASSES D4. The bad solution keeps the fixed-width rows wider than the mobile viewport with margin:0 so overflow persists (D6), drops the inspector selector (D2), shingles the chips with negative margins into an illegible near-opaque panel that buries the scene (D3), and freezes the 'Active layer' readout to a stale module-init snapshot so clicking a tab highlights it but never updates the readout (D4). WebGL renders headless via swiftshader; GL driver ReadPixels messages are console warnings (not errors) and are ignored by the console gate.

metadata.selected_repo_reason: Vite/TypeScript Three.js WebGL X-Ray Visualizer whose fixed-canvas overlay naturally hosts an X-Ray Layer selector HUD; Repair/regression_continuity fix of a canvas-independent HUD defect set (mobile/tablet overflow, missing cross-view selector, stale layer readout, illegible shingled panel) that preserves the shader scene and E-key interaction.
